PullRequest.Title: agentHost: harden canvas icon reads against races and oversized images
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #348466. Addresses the review on that PR, which arrived after it was queued to merge.

### Changes

- **Icons from any host.** Clients now reject a canvas icon whose PNG header declares an empty image or more than 4 megapixels, the host's own limit. A remote or third-party host can send icons without going through VS Code's icon loader, and a small, highly compressed PNG can declare a huge image. The host loader and the client share the limit.
- **Case-only sibling folders.** The icon loader compares the canonical icon and extension paths exactly. It used to ignore case off Linux, so on a case-sensitive macOS volume an icon linked into a sibling folder such as `DEMO` passed as inside `demo`.
- **Listings that change while icons are read.** `listCanvases` checks the registry generation again after reading icons, so a listing its extensions reloaded, or its runtime handed off, during the reads is withheld instead of returned as current.
- **Overlapping icon reads.** Only the latest icon read of a canvas shows its image, and it applies while the canvas still declares that icon. An older read that finished last used to overwrite the newer image.
- **Icon refreshes during restoration.** An update that only shows a new icon no longer looks like a close to the background reopen of a handed-over canvas, which used to leave it unavailable. A close, changed input, or a replaced runtime still cancels the reopen. An unavailable canvas also keeps its icon path, so its icon can still be refreshed.

### Validation

On this branch, rebased on current `main`:

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` with `copilotAgentSession`, `copilotCanvasIcons`, `agentCanvasIconMeta` and `agentHostCanvas`: passed (1763 passing, 1 pending). The pending test needs a case-sensitive file system; it runs on Linux CI.
- Before the rebase, on #348466's head: the 14 suites #348466 touched passed (5093 passing), and so did `copilotNativeExtensions` (3 passing), `npm run oxlint -- <changed files>`, and `npm run valid-layers-check`.
- The new tests for the reload during listing, overlapping reads, icon refresh during restoration, and oversized dimensions each fail without their fix.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The registry-change call path, 350,000-character icon bound, strong current-map root, WeakMap value semantics, and explicit ancestry traversal are all directly visible. The exact number of repeated icon changes varies by workflow, but the retention mechanism and linear scaling are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Historical canvas projection objects and icon data-URI strings retained in memory
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retention grows linearly with the number of successful changed-icon refreshes for each open canvas (up to eight projected canvases), rather than remaining bounded to the current projection.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained memory and increasing GC pressure over the session lifetime
Findings.PreviousBehavior: An icon refresh replaced the projection in `_canvasByInstanceId`; once in-flight users released the old projection, prior canvas states and their icon data URIs were collectible.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each successful icon change now stores `shown -> current` in a WeakMap before `shown` becomes the strongly held current projection. On the next change, the new current points to the previous current, creating a backward chain.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_canvasIconUpdateBases.set(shown, current)` at line 6141 links every replacement to its predecessor, and line 6142 makes `shown` strongly reachable from `_canvasByInstanceId`; repeated changed icons therefore retain all predecessors through WeakMap values.
Findings.Title: Flatten icon-update ancestry instead of retaining every prior icon
Findings.Impact: A long-lived session whose canvas extension is repeatedly reloaded with changing icon contents retains every historical icon, causing steadily growing agent-host memory and GC pressure; extension development/hot reload can accumulate roughly one up-to-350k-character data URI per refresh per open canvas.
Findings.Evidence: `_revalidateCanvasIcons` invokes `_showCanvasIcon` for every open canvas on each registry-change event. A changed icon reaches this line and each projection contains its canvas metadata, including a data URI allowed up to `MAX_CANVAS_ICON_DATA_URI_LENGTH` (350,000 characters). WeakMap keys are weak, but their values are strongly retained while the key is live: the current projection is live in `_canvasByInstanceId`, its value retains the previous projection, that previous projection is itself a key whose value retains the next predecessor, and so on. `_isCurrentCanvasProjection` confirms the code intentionally walks this full chain. There is no per-canvas chain bound until the projection is replaced for another reason, closed, or the session is cleared.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep ancestry bounded: map each icon-only replacement directly to the canonical/root projection needed by restoration (or use a stable projection/version token), rather than to the immediately previous projection, so intermediate states and old icon strings become collectible.

Scenarios.Scenario: List canvas definitions for customization/editor inventory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Two control-plane RPCs (`canvas.list` and `extensions.list`) complete in parallel, followed by all declared icon reads; those icon reads remain on the returned definition snapshot's critical path. The new generation check runs only after those reads and can reject a stale snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List canvas declarations and extensions through control-plane RPCs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two concurrent RPCs per listing request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two RPCs were already issued in parallel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must finish before definition construction proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve, inspect, open, stat, and on cold/change read each declared PNG icon
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One load per canvas declaration with an icon; filesystem calls occur per distinct load, while the 64-entry LRU only avoids byte reading/encoding on a warm unchanged file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same loader and per-definition icon reads were already on this path; the new override delegates to it in production.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All icon loads must settle before `listCanvases` returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of declared canvases in the runtime response; one icon load per declaration with an icon path, grouped neither across definitions nor paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two RPCs run concurrently, then `Promise.all` starts icon loads concurrently for all returned canvases. No new limiter or serialization is introduced by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `CopilotCanvasIconLoader` has a 64-entry LRU keyed by canonical icon path. Warm entries still perform path discovery, realpath, lstat, open, and handle stat, but skip file-byte reading and Base64 encoding when mtime and size match. The diff does not change keys, eviction, negative caching, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the RPC and filesystem call path and in the absence of new production boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime declaration counts and filesystem latency vary; the diff neither raises cardinality nor adds a boundary. A generation change can discard completed work and request a fresh snapshot, but registry changes already invalidate/publish and the retry is required to avoid returning stale inventory.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the post-read generation validation adds constant work and intentional stale-result rejection, while production boundary count and concurrency are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh icons for open or unavailable canvases after a canvas registry change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The registry-change handler publishes inventory invalidation synchronously, then launches icon revalidation without awaiting it. Filesystem reads are therefore off the event handler's immediate critical path, but completed changed icons publish canvas state and retained projections live for the session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate each projected canvas icon through path discovery, canonicalization, metadata checks, and possible file read
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to eight icon loads per registry-change event; overlapping events can have multiple loads in flight per canvas, though only the latest result applies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Open canvases with icon paths were already revalidated on registry changes. The diff newly preserves icon paths for unavailable canvases, extending the existing load to those entries, but the total remains capped at eight and off the immediate critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the synchronous registry event path, but consumes filesystem capacity and publishes state when complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to `MAX_PROJECTED_CANVASES` (8) projected canvases per event, multiplied by registry-change frequency and successful changed-icon refreshes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fire-and-forget icon load is launched per eligible projected canvas; up to eight loads per event can overlap, and overlapping events can overlap further. The new per-instance read sequence suppresses obsolete results but does not cancel their I/O.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged icons use the loader's 64-entry LRU after filesystem metadata validation. Changed mtime/size causes reread and a new data URI. The latest-read map coalesces only result application, not underlying filesystem work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence that each changed icon appends a strongly retained predecessor through the new WeakMap chain and that registry events invoke this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry changes and actual icon-content changes are infrequent for most users but can be repeated during extension development. The exact retained bytes depend on icon lengths; each accepted data URI may be up to 350,000 characters.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable memory regression: the new ancestry chain retains all historical icon-bearing projections and scales linearly with changed-icon refreshes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore handed-over canvases while icon refreshes race with restoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconciliation awaits `canvas.listOpen`, may await `canvas.list`, then each background reopen awaits extension status and `canvas.open`; icon refreshes remain asynchronous. The new ancestry lookup is synchronous before opening and after RPC completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List open canvases, list declared canvases, read extension state, and reopen missing canvases
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listOpen per reconciliation, at most one declaration list, then extension/open calls per missing canvas (up to eight).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reconciliation and reopen boundaries existed; direct projection identity checks previously avoided ancestry traversal and did not retain historical icon projections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The list calls gate reconciliation; each per-canvas open is background work. The new ancestry check gates whether those existing per-canvas calls proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of handed-over/missing canvases, capped by eight, and the number of icon-only replacements that occurred while each original projection remains the restoration identity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Missing canvases are started as background reopen operations from the loop; per-canvas RPC sequencing remains unchanged. Icon reads can overlap those operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Icon refresh uses the same filesystem LRU. Restoration RPCs have no new cache or coalescing behavior in this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed identity mechanism and unchanged RPC cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normally only a small number of icon refreshes occur during one restore, so traversal CPU is small; the memory chain can outlive restoration and continue growing during the session.
Scenarios.Verdict: The RPC scheduling is not a regression, but the ancestry implementation used to preserve restoration identity is the source of the reported unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Validate icon metadata received by a client before rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validation runs synchronously when reading canvas icon metadata. The existing bounded full-string Base64 regex remains dominant; the diff additionally decodes only the fixed 32-character header prefix and reads width/height before an icon can be returned for rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of icon candidates examined, each capped at 350,000 characters; the new work per candidate is fixed-size after the pre-existing full-string validation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per metadata read; no concurrency or scheduling change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache exists on this validation path, before or after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct helper implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Call frequency depends on canvas state publication/rendering, but incremental work is constant-size and rejects oversized decoded bitmaps before the rendering boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the added header decode is bounded constant work and prevents potentially very large downstream image-decoder allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load and canonicalize a canvas PNG from an extension directory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Directory discovery and file checks are awaited by callers. The changed parent comparison and shared dimension helper execute synchronously after existing filesystem operations/file read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe extension entry modules while walking ancestors, canonicalize icon/directory, inspect/open/stat/read the icon
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Entry-module stats scale with ancestor depth; one canonicalization/inspection sequence and at most one file read per load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All filesystem operations and their ordering already existed; the diff only makes the canonical path comparison case-sensitive and reuses the shared constant-time dimension predicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by icon-listing and icon-refresh callers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Ancestor depth during extension-directory discovery and PNG byte size up to the existing byte cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-load steps are sequential except the two realpath calls, which remain parallel; cross-load concurrency is controlled by callers and unchanged here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing 64-entry LRU and mtime/size validation are unchanged. No new negative-cache state or invalidation behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no boundary was added or moved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and ancestor-depth costs vary, but none are increased by the changed comparison/helper.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and traced canvas-definition listing, registry-driven icon refresh, canvas handoff restoration, host icon filesystem loading, and client metadata validation. Reported one introduced unbounded-retention issue in the icon-update ancestry chain. The remaining changes add bounded constant-time validation or preserve existing bounded RPC/filesystem fan-out without a reportable regression.
